findings.title: Unrelated change to how the dev:cron script runs
findings.body: `dev:cron` switches from `ts-node` to `npx tsx`. This has nothing to do with the calendar cache feature. It changes shared dev tooling, and `npx` may download a package version that isn't pinned. Revert it or move it to a separate PR.

findings.title: `sed -i ''` only works with macOS sed and fails on GNU/Linux
findings.body: With GNU sed, `sed -i '' -E "s|...|" file` reads `''` as the script and the substitution as a file name. The command errors out, and `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated, yet the script still prints "Updated". Use a portable form such as `sed -E "s|...|" "$ENV_FILE" > tmp && mv tmp "$ENV_FILE"`. Also, this new dev script is outside the request's scope.

findings.title: Empty-data updateMany adds a write to every cache refresh and may not bump updatedAt
findings.body: Every cache refresh now runs `updateMany(..., {})` on all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential. With empty `data`, Prisma may skip the `@updatedAt` bump, so this could be a no-op. Even if it works, the UI never reads it: the cache status comes from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` through `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`. It also adds a bulk write on the webhook path, and that write can fail the refresh after the cache is already saved. Remove the write, or set `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly if something actually needs it.

findings.title: Unused `updatedAt`/`googleChannelId` fields added to the required UserWithCalendars type
findings.body: `UserWithCalendars` now requires `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on every selected calendar, and `user.ts` selects them. Nothing in the reviewed code reads them, because cache status comes from CalendarCache. Any other place that builds a `UserWithCalendars` must now supply these fields or it fails the type-check. This looks like a leftover from an earlier attempt. Revert these changes, together with the matching select in `user.ts`.

findings.title: Broken calendars can no longer be removed when connection modification is disabled
findings.body: In the calendar-error branch, the old code showed the disconnect button whenever the credential was not a delegation credential, even if connection modification was disabled. Now `disableConnectionModification` is passed in, so when it is true (for example in a disabled scope) a user with a broken credential gets no remove action there. The request does not ask for this change. If it isn't intended, keep the old error-branch behaviour by not passing the flag here.

findings.title: Hand-added `DEFAULT NOW()` probably doesn't match the Prisma schema, which causes migration drift.
findings.body: The header comment is the one Prisma writes when it generates a column with no default. This means `schema.prisma` probably declares `updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt` without `@default(now())`, and the `DEFAULT NOW()` was added to the SQL by hand. With that mismatch, the next `prisma migrate dev` sees drift and generates a migration that drops the default. `migrate diff` and drift checks in CI will also flag it. Fix: add `@default(now())` to the field in `schema.prisma` so the schema matches this SQL, and remove the outdated warning comment. I couldn't see the schema.prisma hunk, so this depends on how the field is declared there.

findings.title: Access-denied path throws a plain Error, which tRPC returns as a 500
findings.body: A missing credential, or one owned by someone else, throws a generic `Error`. tRPC returns that as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR and logs it as a server fault. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or FORBIDDEN) so the client gets the correct error code.

findings.title: Backfill makes existing cache rows look freshly updated.
findings.body: `DEFAULT NOW()` sets `updatedAt` to the migration time for every existing `CalendarCache` row. The new `cacheUpdatedAt` status in the UI will then report every old cache entry as updated at deploy time until the entry is next written, which misstates how fresh it is. A better backfill would use an existing timestamp column, such as `expiresAt` minus the TTL, or would clear the old rows.
